name: sender
title: A high-volume sender
summary: The relay's shape, for a server that sends a great deal - newsletters, notifications, receipts - and is judged by the large providers on its bounce and complaint rates. Everything the relay sets, and more deliveries at once, a ceiling per destination and per sending domain, the feedback loops read so that one complaint suppresses the address, a hard bounce suppressed for good, and the reports receivers send about this server kept for a year.
steps: Warm a new sending address up: start with a few hundred messages a day to each large provider and double it every few days while the bounce and complaint rates stay low. No setting does this; the per-destination ceiling below only keeps a burst from undoing it.
Register a feedback loop with each large provider, and name the mailbox the reports arrive at in the complaint settings (mailbox): until then no complaint is ever read.
Set TlsRptFromAddress to a mailbox here, so that the TLS reports this server owes the domains that ask for them are sent, and publish an MTA-STS policy for each sending domain.
Decide who may relay, and switch DKIM signing on per domain, as for the relay.

entries.name: maxdelivertythreads
entries.why: a high-volume sender's queue drains in minutes rather than hours

entries.name: MaxOutboundConnsPerDestination
entries.why: twenty sessions to one destination at most, spreading a send without looking like a flood

entries.name: MaxOutboundPerDestinationPerMinute
entries.why: at most two messages a second to one destination, so that a burst cannot undo an address's warm-up

entries.name: MaxOutboundConnsPerTenant
entries.why: one sending domain cannot take every delivery and hold up the others' mail

entries.name: BounceSuppressionExpiryDays
entries.why: a hard-bounced address stays suppressed until somebody removes it, because a sender judged on its bounce rate never writes to it again

entries.name: ComplaintProcessingEnabled
entries.why: the abuse reports the providers send are read and counted per domain and per account

entries.name: ComplaintSuppressionThreshold
entries.why: one complaint suppresses the address: the reader pressed the spam button and did not want the mail

entries.name: ComplaintRetentionDays
entries.why: six months of complaints, as shipped, which is longer than any rate is measured over

entries.name: DomainReportRetentionDays
entries.why: the DMARC and TLS reports receivers send about this server are kept a year, as shipped

entries.name: MtaStsHostingEnabled
entries.why: the web services serve each domain's MTA-STS policy, so receivers can hold this server's mail to TLS as well

entries.name: MessageTraceRetentionDays
entries.why: six months of delivery attempts, because a sender is asked about a campaign long after it went

entries.name: AlertsEnabled
entries.why: a listed address, a filling queue or a rising bounce rate is mailed to whoever is named to receive alerts
